fact: Malawi24 reports that improving compliance with the Data Protection Act, 2024 is the aim of MACRA's proposed registration regulations, treating the Act as the law now being complied with.

MACRA, through its Head of Data Protection Daniel Chiwoni, runs the consultation on the draft rules, and organisations are to register with the Data Protection Authority; the article gives no separate appointment of the Authority's head or members (published date used, as the article gives none for the status).

MACRA presented Draft Data Protection Regulations, Guidelines and proposed registration fees (K50,000 for small and medium enterprises up to K7 million for the largest controllers and processors, by annual turnover) at a stakeholder consultation workshop; the article is dated 16 July 2026 and gives no separate event date.

Nyasa Times reports that MACRA, acting as the country's designated Data Protection Authority, convened a stakeholder consultation on draft data protection regulations in Lilongwe, with Daniel Chiwoni as its Head of Data Protection.

The Data Protection Authority held a stakeholder consultation on draft data protection regulations, proposing registration fees for significant data controllers and processors of K50,000 to K7 million by annual turnover, before the regulations are finalised.
ITWeb Africa reports the consultation was part of MACRA's mandate as Malawi's Data Protection Authority, and names Dan Chiwoni as head of data protection at the DPA.
ITWeb Africa describes the consultation as another step in MACRA's implementation of Malawi's Data Protection Act, treating the Act as the law being implemented.

MACRA consulted stakeholders at the Mount Soche Hotel in Blantyre on Monday 13 July 2026 on draft data protection regulations with annual registration fees for significant controllers and processors (about $29 to over $4,000 by turnover), before finalising them.
TechAfrica News reports that MACRA is working to establish the Data Protection Authority and the Malawi CERT as independent institutions, and that both currently operate under the regulator.

The World Bank, at a meeting in Blantyre, announced renewed technical assistance and capacity building to MACRA for data protection systems and legal and regulatory frameworks, alongside MACRA's effort to make the Data Protection Authority independent.

The Authority (MACRA) drafted the Data Protection (Data Processors Engagement) Regulations, 2025 under section 52 of the Data Protection Act (No. 3 of 2024), marked draft and subject to change, with the minister's name and the notice number blank and dated 6 October 2025.

The guidelines state that the Malawi Communications Regulatory Authority is the designated Data Protection Authority, mandated by the Data Protection Act (No. 3 of 2024) to oversee its implementation, and it is issuing guidance as such.

The Authority published guidelines on personal data breach notifications under sections 36 and 37 of the Act (72-hour notice to the Authority and to data subjects, record keeping); the document reports no decision or sanction.
The Authority issued breach notification guidelines under its section 5(2)(a) mandate, dated 22 October 2025.

The guideline states that the Malawi Communications Regulatory Authority is the designated Data Protection Authority under the Data Protection Act (No. 3 of 2024), responsible for overseeing the Act, and it issues the guideline in that role.

The guideline states the Act applies at once to non-Malawi controllers and to Malawi controllers of significant importance (over 10,000 data subjects), who must register and pay fees, while other Malawi controllers and processors are exempt under section 53 until 2 June 2026 and must comply from 3 June 2026.

The Authority published a compliance guideline and checklist covering the Act's duties, data subject rights, breach notice and cross-border transfers, and a registration requirement for controllers of significant importance; no decision or sanction is reported.
The Authority issued a compliance guideline and checklist for the Act, dated 17 October 2025.

The terms of reference for the World Bank-funded Digital Malawi Acceleration Project describe the Data Protection Authority as a unit still to be established within MACRA, with its structure, staffing, operations manual and enforcement framework to be designed by a consultant over up to five months.

The Public Private Partnership Commission issued terms of reference (contract MW-PPPC-502049-CS-QCBS, dated October 2025, no day given) to procure a consultancy to operationalize the Data Protection Authority and draft regulations, codes of practice and guidelines under the Act.

The Data Protection Act, 2024 (Act No. 3 of 2024) was assented to by the President on 31 January 2024 and published on 2 February 2024, and under section 1 it comes into operation on a date the Minister appoints by Gazette notice; this document records no such notice.

Section 4 of the Act designates the Malawi Communications Regulatory Authority as the Data Protection Authority, with independence from direction, and sections 5 and 6 give it enforcement functions and power to issue compliance orders; the document does not say the authority has begun acting under the Act.

The Data Protection Act, 2024 (Act No. 3 of 2024) was passed in Parliament on 7 December 2023, assented by the President on 31 January 2024 and published on 2 February 2024; section 1 brings it into operation on a date the Minister appoints by Gazette notice, and the document names no commencement date.

Section 4 designates the Malawi Communications Regulatory Authority as the Data Protection Authority, to act independently of any person's direction; the document records no appointment of members or start of operations as the authority under the Act.
The deck lists the Data Protection Act, 2023 among the supporting legal frameworks for the financial sector; it does not say whether it has commenced.

Nyasa Times reports MACRA, with a named head of data protection, is moving to enforce the Data Protection Act of 2024, with mandatory data controller and processor fees taking effect on 1 September 2026.
MACRA serves as Malawi's Data Protection Authority, led by Dan Chiwoni, and trained postal and courier operators in Blantyre.
The authority ran a sensitisation meeting for courier operators in Blantyre and warned of penalties ahead of stricter enforcement of the Data Protection Act.

247Malawi reports that a MACRA board director spoke of the Data Protection Act of 2024 as the new law whose enactment created specific mandates for data controllers; the report does not say whether it has commenced.
247Malawi reports that the Malawi Communications Regulatory Authority (MACRA) is intensifying efforts to implement the Data Protection Act.

247Malawi reports that MACRA held a Data Protection Workshop for ministries, departments and agencies in Lilongwe on Wednesday, where a board director warned non-compliance carries mostly administrative liabilities.
Maravi Express (MANA) reports that MACRA has a Head of Data Protection and is drafting two sets of regulations, on registration and on complaints handling, to support Malawi's Data Protection Act.
